source_snapshot.coverage_note: Bounded scoping corpus for conceptual positioning and novelty-risk assessment; not exhaustive and not proof of novelty.

search_directions: human-AI co-creation with artifacts and relational ontology
software and self-evolving agent feedback loops
inclusion_rules: include primary papers, peer-reviewed proceedings, author manuscripts, or normative standards with direct conceptual relevance
include recent nearest-neighbor frameworks that explicitly model artifacts in human-AI co-creation
include empirical or formal work for attribution, incentive, and gaming boundary conditions
record the actual reading level and do not treat metadata-only discovery as evidentiary support
exclusion_rules: exclude popular summaries when a primary source is available
exclude sources used only for naming similarity
exclude unverified claims from hidden drafts or implementation plans
exclude production mechanism selection from Phase A
literature_scope.stop_rule: Stop when every substantive cluster has at least two admitted sources except a normative-standard or method-foundation cluster, and at least two recent nearest neighbors explicitly including artifacts have been found; this is sufficient for Draft 0 novelty-risk assessment, not a systematic or exhaustive review.
out_of_scope: legal determination of ownership or compensation rights
selection of a production economic mechanism

constructs.name: human-agent-artifact coevolution
constructs.definition: A multi-level process in which humans and agents generate variations, artifacts retain selected changes through lineage, and downstream use feeds back into subsequent evolution.

constructs.name: governed artifact lineage
constructs.definition: Versioned artifact continuity with explicit derivation, attribution, and revision relations that preserves behavior-defining changes across time.

constructs.name: provenance-aware contribution
constructs.definition: A contribution representation that distinguishes ideas, code, testing, curation, and governance-relevant acts with traceable attribution.

constructs.name: downstream utility observability
constructs.definition: The capacity to observe post-acceptance usage or value signals without treating them as sufficient evidence of entitlement.

constructs.name: economic feedback closure
constructs.definition: A provenance-aware link from accepted contribution and downstream utility signals to later resource availability for subsequent evolution, without selecting a production mechanism.

concept_model.feedback_loop: Human and agent variation -> artifact acceptance and lineage retention -> usage/value observability -> resource feedback for subsequent evolution -> new variation.

contradictions.statement: Artifact inclusion is not a sufficient novelty claim because artifacts already appear in distributed cognition and co-creation frameworks.
Any allocation-linked framing conflicts with the need to avoid selecting a production mechanism in Phase A.

nearest_neighbors.statement: Tensional-field relational ontology is the closest artifact-inclusive conceptual neighbor.
Human-AI Co-Creation: Why, What, and How? is a direct adjacent frame because it already includes artifact as a minimum unit.
Peeling Back the Layers is a naming neighbor and coevolution framing neighbor.

gaps: No direct primary evidence on a tested economic closure for AI-native software evolution.
No empirical evidence that shadow-mode observability alone improves long-run allocation quality.
No direct validation that the proposed construct set is minimally sufficient.

entries.candidate_contribution: A narrower integration of governed artifact lineage, provenance-aware observability, and downstream resource feedback for AI-native software evolution.
entries.uncertainty: Overlap remains with artifact-inclusive co-creation ontologies; novelty depends on the resource-feedback closure and its testable separation from attribution alone.

entries.candidate_contribution: Formal separation of contribution visibility from governance authority and from economic entitlement.
entries.uncertainty: The separation is well motivated but may be more of a synthesis than a new theory.

entries.candidate_contribution: A shadow-mode observability and attribution substrate as a pre-mechanism evaluation environment.
entries.uncertainty: Need evidence that shadow observability reduces later distortion without inducing false confidence.

entries.candidate_contribution: A falsifiable agenda linking lineage completeness, attribution fidelity, and reward-gaming resistance.
entries.uncertainty: The agenda is novel only if it remains mechanism-agnostic and empirically discriminative.

boundary_conditions.statement: Identity assurance is required before interpreting contribution and usage signals as independent.
Visibility of participation does not imply substantive decision authority.
Allocation-like signals are vulnerable to optimization against the metric itself.
Phase A must not specify currency, token, weights, thresholds, emission, burn, transfer, payout, royalty, ownership share, or automatic reward/sanction.
Artifact lineage alone is insufficient to establish novelty because prior work already formalizes provenance and artifact-centered co-creation.

counterarguments.statement: The framework may be a recombination of established ideas in distributed cognition, provenance, and participatory co-creation rather than a new conceptual contribution.
Attribution or reward-like observability can distort behavior and thereby undermine the very signals the framework seeks to use.
Participation data may be measurable without being governance-relevant, so the framework could overstate the link between contribution signals and authority.
The agent-evolution literature already explains feedback-driven adaptation, so the added artifact-centered layer must demonstrate more than descriptive richness.

limitations.statement: No production economic mechanism is selected or evaluated.
Novelty is calibrated only against the admitted nearest-neighbor set, not proven exhaustively.
The framework remains conceptual; no empirical validation is claimed.
Contribution valuation is not generalized across all artifact types or communities.
Governance authority and entitlement remain intentionally underspecified.
